g1.label: 1. integrity
g1.why: Integrity is about honesty and strong moral standards.

g2.label: 2. framework
g2.why: A framework is the underlying structure of rules that guides decisions.

g3.label: 3. bias
g3.why: Bias is an unfair leaning for or against something.

g4.label: 4. implications
g4.why: Implications are the knock-on effects of a decision.

g5.label: 5. transparency
g5.why: Transparency means working openly, so others can see how decisions are made.

g6.label: 6. equity
g6.why: Equity is fair and just treatment, not speed of learning.

g7.label: 7. implement
g7.why: To implement is to put a plan into action.

g8.label: 8. disclose
g8.why: To disclose is to reveal information — the opposite of keeping it private.

g1.label: 1. difficult questions about the ___ use of AI
g1.why: The sentence is about right and wrong in using AI, so “ethical”.

g2.label: 2. traditional forms of ___
g2.why: The concern is whether traditional assessment still works when AI can write essays.

g3.label: 3. institutions have developed ___
g3.why: Policies are the official rules institutions write in response.

g4.label: 4. provided they ___ the use
g4.why: Students may use AI as long as they acknowledge — openly declare — that they did.

g5.label: 5. AI ___ tools
g5.why: Detection tools are the software that tries to spot AI-written work.

g6.label: 6. questions about fairness and ___
g6.why: Wrongly flagging students raises the question of who is accountable.

g7.label: 7. can enhance student ___
g7.why: Autonomy is independent learning — what supporters say AI increases.

g8.label: 8. think at a deep, ___ level
g8.why: The worry is that over-reliance weakens deep, critical thinking.
